title: A ring buffer reuses freed slots and refuses a push when full

steps.title: Two cursors and a length on five slots
steps.line: Head and tail both start at slot 0; length tells empty from full.
steps.caption: Head is the next value to pop; tail is the next slot to write. Both start at slot 0 and meet again when the ring is full, so length is what tells empty from full. The middle of the ring shows the buffer’s own three fields.
steps.picture: A ring of five slots: slot 0 empty, slot 1 empty, slot 2 empty, slot 3 empty, slot 4 empty. The head arrow points at slot 0 and the tail arrow at slot 0; the middle reads head 0, tail 0, length 0.; A card: Operation: –, Result: –; Code, 14 lines.

steps.title: Five pushes fill the ring
steps.line: Tail is back at 0 with head; only length 5 says full.
steps.caption: Each push outlines the slot at tail, copies v into it, then moves tail on modulo five and adds one to length. After five pushes tail is back at 0 with head, and only length, 5, says the ring is full.
steps.picture: A ring of five slots: slot 0 holds 1, slot 1 holds 2, slot 2 holds 3, slot 3 holds 4, slot 4 holds 5. The head arrow points at slot 0 and the tail arrow at slot 0; the middle reads head 0, tail 0, length 5. Slot 4 is outlined in the tail colour, where 5 was just written. push(v) holds 5.; A card: Operation: push 5, Result: ok; Code, 14 lines. Focused: 3: data[tail] = v; 4: tail = (tail + 1) % capacity; 5: length++. New in this step: A ring of five slots: slot 0 holds 1, slot 1 holds 2, slot 2 holds 3, slot 3 holds 4, slot 4 holds 5. The head arrow points at slot 0 and the tail arrow at slot 0; the middle reads head 0, tail 0, length 5. Slot 4 is outlined in the tail colour, where 5 was just written. push(v) holds 5.; A card: Operation: push 5, Result: ok.

steps.title: Two pops free slots 0 and 1
steps.line: Head moves on to 2; tail stays at 0 for the next push.
steps.caption: The two pops copy the values in slots 0 and 1 out to the tray and clear both slots, then head moves on to 2. Tail stays at 0, so the next push goes into slot 0, the first of the two outlined slots the pops freed.
steps.picture: A ring of five slots: slot 0 empty, slot 1 empty, slot 2 holds 3, slot 3 holds 4, slot 4 holds 5. The head arrow points at slot 2 and the tail arrow at slot 0; the middle reads head 2, tail 0, length 3. Slot 0 is outlined in the head colour, popped and now empty. Slot 1 is outlined in the head colour, popped and now empty. Under the ring, after “popped:”: 1, 2.; A card: Operation: pop twice, Result: returned 1, 2; Code, 14 lines. Focused: 9: const v = data[head]; 10: data[head] = null; 11: head = (head + 1) % capacity; and 2 more. New in this step: A ring of five slots: slot 0 empty, slot 1 empty, slot 2 holds 3, slot 3 holds 4, slot 4 holds 5. The head arrow points at slot 2 and the tail arrow at slot 0; the middle reads head 2, tail 0, length 3. Slot 0 is outlined in the head colour, popped and now empty. Slot 1 is outlined in the head colour, popped and now empty. Under the ring, after “popped:”: 1, 2.; A card: Operation: pop twice, Result: returned 1, 2.

steps.title: The tail wraps into freed slots
steps.line: 6 and 7 go into slots 0 and 1; no stored value moves.
steps.caption: Tail wrapped to 0 after the fifth push, so 6 and 7 are copied into slots 0 and 1 and no stored value moves. Length is back to 5, with head and tail both at 2.
steps.picture: A ring of five slots: slot 0 holds 6, slot 1 holds 7, slot 2 holds 3, slot 3 holds 4, slot 4 holds 5. The head arrow points at slot 2 and the tail arrow at slot 2; the middle reads head 2, tail 2, length 5. Slot 1 is outlined in the tail colour, where 7 was just written. push(v) holds 7. Under the ring, after “popped:”: 1, 2.; A card: Operation: push 7, Result: ok; Code, 14 lines. Focused: 3: data[tail] = v; 4: tail = (tail + 1) % capacity; 5: length++. New in this step: A ring of five slots: slot 0 holds 6, slot 1 holds 7, slot 2 holds 3, slot 3 holds 4, slot 4 holds 5. The head arrow points at slot 2 and the tail arrow at slot 2; the middle reads head 2, tail 2, length 5. Slot 1 is outlined in the tail colour, where 7 was just written. push(v) holds 7. Under the ring, after “popped:”: 1, 2.; A card: Operation: push 7, Result: ok.

steps.title: push 6 throws Full before changing anything
steps.line: The first line of push finds length === capacity, both 5.
steps.caption: push checks length === capacity on its first line, so with length 5 it throws Full before writing a slot or moving either cursor. The 6 is crossed out short of slot 0 and goes to the refused tray, and head, tail and length do not change.

The head arrow points at slot 0 and the tail arrow at slot 0; the middle reads head 0, tail 0, length 5. Slot 0 is outlined in red, where push 6 would have gone. push(v) holds 6. Under the ring, after “refused, Full:”: 6, crossed out.; A card: Operation: push 6, Result: Full (marked); Code, 14 lines. Focused: 2: if (length === capacity) throw new Full(). steps.title: push 7 is refused and the ring is unchanged
steps.line: Head, tail and length still read 0, 0 and 5.
steps.caption: push 7 is refused the same way and joins 6 in the refused tray. The ring still holds 1 to 5, and head, tail and length still read 0, 0 and 5.
